content: Naproxen sodium is an analgesic and anti-inflammatory medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of conditions such as ankylosing spondylitis, bursitis, acute gout, osteoarthritis, pain, primary dysmenorrhea, rheumatoid arthritis, and tendinitis. Common adverse reactions include edema, ecchymosis, pruritus, rash, abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn, nausea, dizziness, headache, somnolence, ototoxicity, tinnitus, and dyspnea. For ankylosing spondylitis, the recommended dosage of naproxen sodium is 275 or 550 mg taken twice daily, in the morning and evening. Dosage adjustments should be made based on clinical response, and lower doses may suffice for long-term administration. A dose of 1650 mg/day may be used for up to six months in patients tolerating lower doses well, but patients should be monitored to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks. For controlled-release naproxen sodium, the recommended dose is 750 to 1000 mg orally once daily. If the clinical response is inadequate, the dose may be increased to 1500 mg once daily for a limited period. The smallest effective dose should always be used. For bursitis, the initial recommended dose is 550 mg, followed by 550 mg every 12 hours or 275 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 1375 mg on the first day of treatment and 1100 mg per day thereafter. Controlled-release naproxen sodium for bursitis is dosed at 1000 mg orally once daily, with the option to increase to 1500 mg once daily for a limited time if pain relief is inadequate. Once adequate pain control is achieved, the dose should not exceed 1000 mg daily. For acute gout, the recommended initial dose is 825 mg, followed by 275 mg every 8 hours until the attack subsides. Controlled-release naproxen sodium for acute gout is dosed at 1000 to 1500 mg orally on the first day, followed by 1000 mg once daily until the attack resolves. For osteoarthritis, the recommended dose is 275 or 550 mg twice daily, with adjustments based on clinical response. Long-term administration may require lower doses, and a dose of 1650 mg/day may be used for up to six months in patients tolerating lower doses well. Controlled-release naproxen sodium is dosed at 750 to 1000 mg orally once daily, with the option to increase to 1500 mg once daily for a limited time if needed. For mild to moderate pain, acute tendinitis, and bursitis, the recommended dose is 550 mg initially, followed by 550 mg every 12 hours or 275 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 1375 mg on the first day and 1100 mg per day thereafter. Controlled-release naproxen sodium for mild to moderate pain is dosed at 1000 mg orally once daily, with the option to increase to 1500 mg once daily for a limited time if needed. For over-the-counter use, naproxen sodium (Aleve®) is recommended at an initial dose of 220 to 440 mg, followed by 220 mg every 8 to 12 hours as needed. The daily dose should not exceed 440 mg in any 8 to 12-hour period or 660 mg in 24 hours. Therapy duration should not exceed 10 days unless directed by a physician. For primary dysmenorrhea, the recommended dose is 550 mg initially, followed by 550 mg every 12 hours or 275 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 1375 mg on the first day and 1100 mg per day thereafter. Controlled-release naproxen sodium is dosed at 1000 mg orally once daily, with the option to increase to 1500 mg once daily for a limited time if needed. For rheumatoid arthritis, the recommended dose is 275 or 550 mg twice daily, with adjustments based on clinical response. Morning and evening doses do not need to be equal. Long-term administration may require lower doses, and a dose of 1650 mg/day may be used for up to six months in patients tolerating lower doses well. Controlled-release naproxen sodium is dosed at 750 to 1000 mg orally once daily, with the option to increase to 1500 mg once daily for a limited time if needed. For pediatric patients aged 12 years and older, over-the-counter naproxen sodium (Aleve®) is dosed at 220 to 440 mg initially, followed by 220 mg every 8 to 12 hours as needed. The daily dose should not exceed 440 mg in any 8 to 12-hour period or 660 mg in 24 hours. Therapy duration should not exceed 10 days unless directed by a physician. For juvenile arthritis in children aged 2 years and older, the recommended total daily dose is approximately 10 mg/kg, given in two divided doses (5 mg/kg twice daily). Naproxen suspension is generally recommended for children to allow for more flexible dosing. Naproxen sodium may cause severe allergic reactions, particularly in individuals allergic to aspirin. Symptoms include hives, facial swelling, asthma (wheezing), shock, skin reddening, rash, and blisters. If an allergic reaction occurs, discontinue use and seek medical attention immediately. Naproxen sodium contains an NSAID, which may cause severe stomach bleeding. Risk factors include age 60 or older, a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding problems, concurrent use of blood thinners or steroids, use of other NSAIDs, consumption of three or more alcoholic drinks daily, and exceeding the recommended dose or duration of use. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. Naproxen sodium should not be used during the last three months of pregnancy unless directed by a physician, as it may cause complications for the unborn child or during delivery. Patients should take naproxen sodium with food or milk if stomach upset occurs. The risk of heart attack or stroke may increase with higher doses or prolonged use. If symptoms such as fainting, vomiting blood, bloody or black stools, persistent stomach pain, or difficulty swallowing occur, discontinue use and consult a physician. Naproxen sodium should be stored out of reach of children. In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately.
